A.why: Peaked hood and lone raked shoulder spur give a real outline; dark slabs separate it from iron, but red seams vanish from the ARPG camera.
A.fix: Widen two or three red seams so they read from above; grow the shoulder spur into a seated stepped basalt shard and merge the small chest slabs.

B.why: Heavy golem mass with a tall crown and visible red edges, but a bright yellow visor band reads as brass/studded and two shapes compete.
B.fix: Make the visor slit red or dark; commit to either the crown or the stepped shoulders.

C.why: Rock outcrops breaking from the plate fit the brief, but they are small, pale tan and look like loose debris; the body is a plain black box.
C.fix: One large dark crag seated into a pauldron or helm, with a red seam at its root.

D.why: Gold baldric and yellow trim read as studded/brass; light grey plate tops read as iron from above; no silhouette idea.
D.fix: Remove the gold, darken the tops to basalt, and add a single silhouette idea with red seams between slabs.

E.why: Red seams carry from the ARPG camera and the raked helm shard is a single strong silhouette no other family has.
E.fix: Make the shard dark faceted basalt with a red root seam (not pale bone/iron); drop the yellow slit and the pale chest square.

F.why: Best fit and on-palette seams, but uniform boxes read as stacked crates with no silhouette idea; yellow visor slit reads as brass.
F.fix: Step or taper the helm into a slab crown, make the slit red, and offset one or two slabs with seams in the gaps.

notes: E and A lead on silhouette (helm shard, hood and spur). Yellow or gold appears in B, D, E and F and reads as brass/studded: remove it everywhere. Red seams need to be thicker and run across slab faces, not only as edge trim, to survive the high camera. C has the best brief idea (rock outcrops) but the weakest execution.
